extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent holders, patent attorneys/agents, and IP office officials in Indonesia
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing, substantive examination, grant/refusal, appeals, transfer, licensing, and compulsory licensing under Indonesian patent law (rules for applicants, holders, and the Ministry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of consulted government institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The government institutions as referred to in section (1) are required to preserve the confidentiality of the Inventions and Application documents being consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Minister consults government institutions during processing of an application, those institutions must keep consulted invention details and application documents confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and fee for request for substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for the substantive examination is submitted in writing to the Minister and subject to a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination will not commence unless a written request is filed with payment of the prescribed fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to file request for substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for substantive examination ... is filed not later than 36 (thirty six) months as from the Filing Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request is not filed within 36 months from the filing date, the application will be deemed withdrawn (unless other provisions apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to file or pay for substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request for substantive examination has not been filed ... or the prescribed fee has not been paid, the Application is deemed to be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Minister must notify the Applicant or Proxy regarding the withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of substantive examination relative to announcement period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request ... is filed before the end of the announcement period ... the substantive examination is conducted after the expiry of the announcement period. If filed after the expiry, substantive examination is conducted after the date of receipt of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing before announcement end delays examination until announcement period expires; filing after triggers examination from receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination requests for divisionals/amendments must be filed together
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for substantive examination of divisional Application or amendment of Application from Patent to simple Patent or vice versa is filed together with the request for divisional Application or amendment of Application ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not filed together, the divisional or amendment is deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for substantive examination when application not announced
rubrics_metrics.description: The substantive examination for Application that is not announced ... is conducted for not later than 6 (six) months as from the date the Minister decides that the Application is not announced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an application is not announced, the office must complete substantive examination within six months of the decision of non-announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fee for substantive examination in non-announced cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The substantive examination as referred to in section (1) is not subject to a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Minister decides an application is not announced and conducts substantive examination under that provision, no fee is charged for that examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners and use of experts in substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examinations are conducted by Examiners. The Minister may request assistance from experts and/or use required facilities from other institutions ... Experts are appointed and dismissed by the Minister. Results of substantive examination conducted by the experts ... are considered same as examination results conducted by the Examiners. The results ... must obtain approval from the Minister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examinations normally done by Examiners; expert input is permitted and treated as equivalent but requires Ministerial approval; further appointment rules via ministerial regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination must follow statutory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examinations are conducted in accordance with the provisions in Article 3 section (1), Article 4, Article 5, Article 7, Article 8, Article 9, Article 25 section (3) and section (4), Article 26, Article 39 section (2), Article 40, and Article 41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must apply the specific substantive legal criteria set out elsewhere in the statute (e.g., patentability requirements referenced in those articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence from foreign/prosecuting offices for Priority Right applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that the substantive examination is conducted to an Application with a Priority Right, the Minister may request required documents ... such as certified copies of letters relevant to results of substantive examination in other countries; certified copies of Patent documents granted abroad; certified copies of decisions for refusal or invalidation; and other prescribed documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with priority claims should be prepared to produce certified foreign prosecution/examination documents; these may influence grant or refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation and use of foreign documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of those document copies ... may be supplemented separately with additional explanation by an Applicant. The documents ... may be used as the grounds for granting or refusing an Application with a Priority Right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can provide explanations alongside foreign documents; foreign decisions or grants can be determinative evidence in Indonesian substantive examination of priority applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minister decision timeline for grant or refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister decides to grant or refuse an Application not later than 30 (thirty) months as from: (a) the date of receipt of the request for substantive examination if the request ... is submitted after the expiry of the announcement period; or (b) the expiry of announcement period ... if a request ... is filed before the expiry of announcement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall outer limit: 30 months from the relevant start point for the Minister to decide to grant or refuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for grant based on substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister grants an Application, if based on the result of substantive examination, the Invention being requested for a Patent complies with the provisions as referred to in Article 54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant requires examiner finding compliance with the statutory substantive provisions incorporated by Article 54.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and patent certificate issuance after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that an Application is granted, the Minister notifies the Applicant or his/her Proxy in writing that the Application is granted a Patent. Within not later than 2 (two) months as from the notification ... the Minister issues a Patent certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a grant decision, the office must issue the patent certificate within two months of notifying the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on withdrawal or modification after grant notification
rubrics_metrics.description: An Applicant may not withdraw the Application or modify the description and claim within the period of time as referred to in section (3) [2 months after notification].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the two-month period until the certificate is issued, the applicant cannot withdraw or change the granted application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and publication of granted patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent that has been granted is recorded and published, except for Patent which concerns the defense and security of the State. The Minister may provide excerpt or copies of Patent documents to parties in need to be subject to fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granted patents are recorded/published (with exceptions) and copies/excerpts available subject to fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent certificate as proof of right and scope defined by claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent Certificate is a proof of right on Patent. The right of Patent ... is determined its scope of protection based on Invention described in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate proves the patent right; claims define the scope of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive effect of patent certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent protection is proven by the issuance of a Patent certificate which is valid retroactively as of the Filing Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate, once issued, gives effect from the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of patent certificate errors and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent holder or Proxy may file for correction ... if there is a data error ... If errors on Patent certificate are constituted as Applicant’s mistakes, the request for correction ... is subject to fees. If data errors ... do not constitute Applicant’s mistakes, the request ... is not subject to fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections allowed; fee liability depends on whether the error is the applicant's fault; name/address modifications are recorded and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification content and procedures on refusal (office action)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Examiner indicates that the Invention ... has not fulfilled the provisions ... the Minister notifies the Applicant ... to comply with the provisions. The notification mentions: (a) the provisions to be fulfilled; and (b) the reasons and references used in substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office deficiency notices must state which statutory provisions are unmet and explain the reasons and references relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timeframe to refusal notification and extension rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Applicant must provide response and/or fulfill the provisions ... not later than 3 (three) months as from the date of notification. The period may be extended for not later than 2 (two) months. The extension may be extended for not later than 1 (one) month after the end of the period and subject to fees. To obtain period extension ... the Applicant must submit a request ... in writing before the period ... is expired. In emergencies, the Applicant may request for extension in another way ... furnished by supporting evidence. The Minister may give period extension ... not later than 6 (six) months after the end of the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard reply period is 3 months with structured extension options (2 months, then 1 more month subject to fees), emergency extensions allowed with evidence, and minister can grant further extension up to 6 months after the end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of no or non-conforming response to notification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Applicant’s response does not in conformity ... within the period of time ... the Minister notifies the Applicant in writing that the Application is refused within the period of not later than 2 (two) months. If the Applicant does not provide response ... the Minister notifies the Applicant in writing that the Application is deemed to be withdrawn within the period of not later than 2 (two) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond or inadequate response leads to refusal or deemed withdrawal; minister must notify within 2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for refusal of divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister refuses: (a) a divisional Application that is filed elapsing the duration as referred to in Article 38 section (2); (b) a claim or claims expanding the scope of protection in a divisional Application ...; and/or (c) an invention which is not a unity of the original Application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisionals filed late, with expanded scope, or lacking unity with the original application are subject to refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal notification must include reasons and consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that Application is refused, the Minister notifies the refusal in writing with reason and consideration to the Applicant or his/her Proxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal letters must state the reasons and considerations for the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of the Patent Appeal Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Appeal Commission holds the duties to receive, examine, and make a decision on: (a) an appeal petition against refused Application; (b) an appeal petition against correction of description, claim, and/or drawings after the Application is granted a Patent; and (c) an appeal petition against the decision to grant a Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission handles appeals on refusal, post-grant corrections, and challenges to grant decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and appointment of Patent Appeal Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure ... comprises of: 1 chairman also acting as a member; 1 vice chairman also acting as a member; and at the most 30 members from: 15 Patent experts; and 15 Examiners. Members ... are appointed and dismissed by the Minister for a period of 3 years and may be re-appointed for 1 subsequent period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission membership limits, balance between experts and examiners, and term (3 years, renewable once).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel formation for appeal examination
rubrics_metrics.description: To examine an appeal petition, the Patent Appeal Commission establishes a panel consisting odd number of a minimum of 3 persons and maximum of 5 persons, who one of which is appointed as the Chairman. The panel is chosen from members ... one of members is an Examiner with minimum rank is Third Level Examiner who does not conduct an examination to said Application. If the panel consists of more than 3 persons, the Examiners ... are less than the total number of panel other than Examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels must be odd (3–5), include at least one suitably-ranked Examiner not previously involved; if panel >3, examiners must be fewer than non-examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for appeal petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal petition may be filed with respect to: Application refusal; correction ... after grant; and/or decision to grant a Patent. Appeal petition is filed in writing by the Applicant or his/her Proxy to Patent Appeal Commission with a copy to the Minister subject to fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be written, filed by applicant/proxy, copy to Minister, and are subject to fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and content limits for appeals against refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal petition with respect to Application refusal is filed not later than 3 (three) months as from the mailing date of the notification for Application refusal. The appeal petition ... objection and grounds against the Application refusal must be described in detail. The grounds ... do not constitute new reasons or explanations that expand the scope of the Invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 3-month filing deadline; appeals must be detailed but cannot introduce new grounds or expand the invention's scope beyond the original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for appeal examination and decision (refusal appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Appeal Commission starts conducting examination ... not later than 1 (one) month as from the date of receipt of said petition. The decision ... is made not later than 9 (nine) months as from the date when the examination begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission must start within one month and issue decision within nine months of starting the examination on refusal appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and follow-up when appeal against refusal is accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Patent Appeal Commission decides to accept the appeal petition with respect to the Application refusal, the Minister follows up by issuing Patent certificate. ... the Minister records and publishes it in the electronic media and/or non-electronic media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance triggers issuance of patent certificate and public recording/publication of the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal on correction after grant: deadlines and permissible corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal petition ... is filed within 3 (three) months ... The correction ... must be limited to: limitation on the scope of claim(s); correction for mistranslation of the description; and/or clarification on the unclear and ambiguous content of the description. Correction ... is not beyond the scope of Invention as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant correction appeals must be filed within 3 months and are limited to narrowing claims, mistranslation fixes, or clarifications that do not extend the original scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for correction appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Appeal Commission starts ... not later than 1 (one) month ... The decision ... is decided for not later than 6 (six) months as from the commencing date of the examination ... If accepted ... the Minister responds by amending the certificate attachment and records/publishes it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission must start within one month; decide within six months; accepted corrections lead to amendment and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal against decision to grant: standing, deadline, and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal petition with respect to the decision to grant a Patent is filed in writing by respected parties or their Proxies ... filed not later than 9 (nine) months as from the date of the notification for granting a Patent. The petition provides complete details of the objection with the reasons with supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties with standing may appeal grants within 9 months and must submit full objections supported by evidence; if the period lapses, the remedy is to file a lawsuit in Commercial Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and outcomes for appeals against grant decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Appeal Commission starts conducting examination ... not later than 1 (one) month ... The decision ... is issued not later than 9 (nine) months as from the date commencing of appeal examination. If the Commission grants the appeal in part, the Minister amends the attachment of the certificate; if it grants all, the Minister revokes the certificate. The decision is recorded and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start within one month, decide within nine months; possible outcomes include amendment or revocation, with required recording/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of appeal decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Appeal Commission is required to send notification letter within a period of 14 (fourteen) Days as from the date of the decision to accept or to refuse: (a) appeal petition with respect to Application refusal; (b) appeal petition for correction ... after granting; and (c) appeal petition with respect to the decision to grant a Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission must notify parties of its decision within 14 days of the decision date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review timelines after Patent Appeal Commission refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant or his/her Proxy may file a lawsuit against the decision to refuse Patent Appeal Commission to the Commercial Court not later than 3 (three) months as from the mailing date of notification for refusal. To the decision of the Commercial Court ... it may only file an appeal to the Supreme Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month window to sue Commission refusals in Commercial Court; further appeal only to the Supreme Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted grounds for transfer of patent rights and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights on a Patent may transfer ... due to: inheritance; donation; testament; waqf; written agreement; or other recognized reasons. The transfer ... must be supplemented by the original Patent documents together with other rights pertaining to the relevant Patent. All forms of transfer ... must be recorded and published subject to fees. Any transfer ... not in accordance ... rights and obligations still remain on the Patent Holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers are permitted for listed legal reasons, require original documents, must be recorded/published (fees apply), and failures in procedure leave rights with the original holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's right to be named preserved on transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of rights does not nullify the right of Inventor to have his/her name and identity included in the Patent certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral right of inventor to be named remains even after transfer of patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to license and scope of licensing agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Patent Holder is entitled to give a License ... pursuant to either an exclusive or non-exclusive Licensing agreement to perform any acts as referred to in Article 19. Licensing Agreement ... may cover all or in parts of acts ... is valid for the term of the License granted and is effective in the entire territory of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent holders may grant exclusive/non-exclusive licenses covering whole or part of rights, valid for the license term and effective throughout Indonesia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default exclusivity of patent exploitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Holder ... is entitled to exclusively exploit his/her Patent, unless agreed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent an agreement, the patent holder retains exclusive exploitation rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited license provisions (public interest/technology transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensing Agreement is prohibited from containing provisions that may damage the Indonesian national interest or to contain restrictions which obstruct the abilities of Indonesian people to transfer, master and develop technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing agreements cannot include terms harmful to national interest or that impede technology transfer/development in Indonesia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation requirement for licensing agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensing Agreement must be recorded and published by the Minister and subject to fees. If a Licensing Agreement is not recorded and published ... the Licensing agreement does not have legal effects on the third party. The Minister refuses a request for recording of Licensing agreement containing provisions as referred to in Article 78.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be effective against third parties, licenses must be recorded/published; the Minister may refuse to record prohibited license terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license is non-exclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License is non-exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any compulsory license granted under the statute will be non-exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for granting a compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License ... is granted ... upon request on the following grounds: (a) Patent Holder has not fulfilled his/her obligation to make products or use the process in Indonesia ... within a period of 36 months after the granting of a Patent; (b) Patent has been implemented ... in any forms and by any manners that harm the public interest; or (c) a Patent as the result of development from a Patent that has been granted earlier cannot be exploited without infringing other protected Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licenses are triggered by non-working, public-interest-harming exploitation, or blocking patents that prevent exploitation of follow-on innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing requests for compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: A request ... on the ground (a) may be filed after the period of 36 months as from the date of granting of a Patent. A request ... on the ground (b) and (c) may be submitted at any time after a Patent is granted. The request for (c) may only be granted if the Patent to be implemented contains novelty that is more advanced than existing Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-working requests limited to after 36 months; public-interest or blocking-innovation grounds may be sought anytime; for blocking patents, the requested patent must be sufficiently novel/advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions Minister requires to grant compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License ... may only be granted ... provided that: (a) the applicant ... can show evidence that he/she has the capability to personally and fully implement the relevant Patent and has facilities to readily implement; (b) the applicant ... has made efforts in a period for not later than 12 months to acquire a License from the Patent Holder on the basis of normal terms and conditions but did not succeed; and (c) the Minister has the opinion that the relevant Patent may be implemented in Indonesia on a feasible economic scale and can be benefit to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting requires demonstration of capacity to implement, documented attempts (up to 12 months) to obtain a license on normal terms, and Ministerial assessment of feasibility/public benefit; supporting institutional statements required for capability evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules when compulsory license for blocking (article 82(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that a compulsory License is filed on the grounds ... point c, thus: (a) the Patent Holder is entitled to mutual Licensing to use the other parties’ Patent under reasonable terms; and (b) the implementation of Patent by Licensee cannot be transferred unless it is transferred together with assignment of the other Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compulsory license is granted because of blocking patents, the patent holder gets cross-licensing rights and the licensee's implementation cannot be transferred separately from the associated patent assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure for compulsory license requests and hearing of patent holder
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination ... is conducted by an ad-hoc expert team appointed by the Minister ... the expert team invites the Patent Holder to have his/her opinion heard. The Patent Holder is required to express his/her opinion not later than 30 (thirty) Days ... If the Patent Holder does not express his/her opinion ... the Patent Holder is deemed to approve the granting of a compulsory License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests are examined by an expert team which must invite and allow the patent holder a 30-day opportunity to respond; silence is treated as approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification timing for decision to grant/suspend/refuse compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister notifies the decision to grant, suspend, or refuse a request for compulsory License to: (a) the applicant ... and (b) the Patent Holder ... The notification ... is communicated not later than 7 (seven) Days as from the date of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office must notify both applicant and patent holder within seven days of deciding on the compulsory license request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and timing of Ministerial decision on granting compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Minister grants a request ... the Minister stipulates a Ministerial Decision ... including the amount of Remuneration and method of payment. The stipulation ... is carried out not later than 90 (ninety) Days as from the requesting date for compulsory License. A period ... excludes the period of suspension to not later than 12 (twelve) months ... Decision ... mentions: (a) that the compulsory License is non-exclusive; (b) the reasons for granting; (c) evidence ...; (d) the period of compulsory License; (e) the amount of Remuneration payable ... and the method of payment; (f) the conditions for termination and matters which may cancel; (g) scope of compulsory License for entire or partial Patent; and (h) other matters necessary to protect interests fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must be detailed (including remuneration, period, scope, termination conditions) and issued within 90 days of request (excluding suspension), with suspension up to 12 months allowed; format details by ministerial regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial challenge of compulsory license decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision of the Minister on the granting of a compulsory License ... may be a subject of a lawsuit to the Commercial Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministerial decisions on compulsory licenses are challengeable in Commercial Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minister may suspend/refuse grant on certain grounds and suspension timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister may suspend or refuse the granting ... on the grounds provided by a recommendation from expert team and declaration from Patent Holder, the prevailing Patent requires time longer than 36 months to be commercially implemented in Indonesia. The suspension ... is provided for a period of 12 (months) ... The Minister stipulates a decision to grant or refuse ... within a period of 14 (fourteen) Days as from the end of date of suspension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minister can suspend consideration for up to 12 months where evidence suggests implementation will need >36 months; after suspension ends, decision must be issued within 14 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration requirement for compulsory licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory Licensee must provide Remuneration to the Patent Holder. Provisions regarding the amount of Remuneration and method of payment ... are regulated by a Ministerial Regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licenses require remuneration to patent holder; exact computation/method left to regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special compulsory license rules for pharmaceuticals (public health)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister may grant a compulsory License to make pharmaceutical products patented in Indonesia to serve a purpose of medication of human diseases; may grant to import supply ... yet has not been feasible to be made in Indonesia; may grant to export pharmaceutical products patented and made in Indonesia to serve ... upon request from developing or least developed countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific public-health oriented compulsory licensing provisions permit manufacture, import, and export for medication purposes and for supplying developing countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and publication obligations for granting compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister is obligated to record the granting of compulsory License in the Patent database and publish it in electronic media and/or non-electronic media. Recording and publishing ... are carried out not later than 30 (thirty) Days as from the date of the stipulation of granting of compulsory License by the Minister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions granting compulsory licenses must be recorded and published within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending copies of decision and public access to excerpts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister sends the copy of decision on granting compulsory License to: (a) applicant ...; (b) Patent Holder ... The sending ... is carried out not later than 30 (thirty) Days ... Every Person may file a request for an excerpt of decision to grant a compulsory License. A request for an excerpt ... must be submitted in writing ... to the Directorate General of Intellectual Property subject to fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies must be sent to the parties within 30 days; third parties may request excerpts subject to fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and effect of compulsory license implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory License is granted to a Licensee for a period of time without exceeding the Patent protection period requested by the Compulsory License. Implementation of Compulsory License by the Licensee is deemed as implementation of a Patent requested on said Compulsory License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License duration cannot exceed remaining patent term; licensee's implementation counts as exploitation of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent holder obligations remain despite compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: The granting of a compulsory License does not release a Patent Holder from the obligation to pay annual fee in accordance with the prevailing legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when a compulsory license is granted, the patent holder must continue statutory obligations such as annual fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions for compulsory licenses on semiconductor technology
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that a compulsory License is related to technology of semi-conductor, the holder of compulsory License may only uses compulsory License for: (a) non-commercial public interest; or (b) action based on court order or decision of relevant agency stating that the implementation of said Patent constitutes a monopoly or unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licenses for semiconductors are tightly limited to non-commercial public interest or court/agency-ordered remedies against monopolistic/unfair practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee cooperation allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of implementing compulsory License, the holder of compulsory License may cooperate with other parties both nationally and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licensees may partner domestically or abroad to implement the licensed technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability of compulsory license (inheritance exception) and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License is not transferrable, except due to inheritance. In the event that a compulsory License is transferred by inheritance, the Ministerial Decision on granting Compulsory License remains in effect to the beneficiary. A compulsory License which is transferred from inheritance ... must be reported to the Minister to be recorded in the patent database and published ... If the beneficiary does not report the transfer ... the Ministerial Decision ... is invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licenses cannot be assigned except via inheritance; inherited transfers must be reported and recorded or the decision becomes invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory license termination grounds and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A compulsory License is terminated because of the expiry of period set forth on the decision ... or due to a decision of the Commercial Court ... Other than expiry and court nullification, a compulsory License may be terminated because of nullification upon request of Patent Holder provided that: (a) the grounds ... no longer exist; (b) the compulsory Licensee has evidently not implemented the compulsory License or has not made appropriate preparations for immediate implementation; or (c) the compulsory Licensee is no longer complying with other terms and conditions. A request for nullification on the grounds (b) may be carried out after compulsory Licensee does not implement ... within 24 (twenty-four) months since the date of decision. Other terms ... may be: payment of Remuneration; or compliance to the scope of License, set forth in the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination can occur on expiry, court nullification, or ministerial nullification for no-longer-existing grounds, non-implementation (24 months), non-payment, or other breaches; ministerial procedures and evidence requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, recording, and restoration on termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister is required to notify the decision on nullification of a compulsory License ... to Patent Holder and Compulsory Licensee. Notification ... is communicated not later than 14 (fourteen) Days as from the issuance date of the Ministerial Decision on nullification. The Minister is required to record the termination ... in the Patent database and publish it ... The record ... is done not later than 14 (fourteen) Days as from the date of terminated compulsory License. Termination ... results in the restoration of the right of Patent Holder to the relevant Patent as from the date of recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minister must notify parties and record/publicize termination within 14 days; restoration of full patent rights occurs as of the recording date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further procedural detail deferred to Ministerial Regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Further provisions regarding terms and procedures for substantive examination / appointment of experts / procedures for appeal petitions / recording of licensing / granting of compulsory License are regulated by a Ministerial Regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many procedural specifics are left to secondary ministerial regulations; practitioners should consult the applicable Ministerial Regulations for detailed rules and forms.
